name: Peripheral Pulmonary Stenosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of stenosis in peripheral branches of the pulmonary artery by echocardiography, angiography, or MRI
Presence of a systolic ejection murmur best heard over the upper left sternal border
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary artery obstruction such as pulmonary valve stenosis or pulmonary hypertension
Identification of associated syndromes such as Williams syndrome or Noonan syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis and clinical murmur with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and clinical correlation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur over upper left sternal border
Reduced peripheral pulmonary artery blood flow detected by imaging
searchTerms: low blood flow in lung arteries

common.symptomName: Fatigue on exertion due to decreased pulmonary perfusion
searchTerms: tiredness with activity from poor lung blood flow
exercise fatigue due to lung perfusion
enlarged right heart muscle on ECG

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort or mild chest pain

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected

rare.symptomName: Syncope due to right heart strain
searchTerms: passing out due to heart stress
syncope related to right heart overload

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to severe stenosis
searchTerms: high lung blood pressure from valve narrowing

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory studies; may show secondary polycythemia in chronic hypoxia
imaging: Echocardiography showing peripheral pulmonary artery narrowing
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming location and severity of stenosis
genetic: Association with genetic syndromes such as Williams syndrome (ELN gene deletion) and Noonan syndrome
other: Electrocardiogram may show right ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Stenosis localized at pulmonary valve rather than peripheral branches
Characteristic valve leaflet abnormalities on echocardiogram
Elevated pulmonary artery pressures without discrete stenotic lesions
Diffuse vascular remodeling rather than focal narrowing

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Signs of right heart failure (jugular venous distension, hepatomegaly, peripheral edema)
references: Gatzoulis MA, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Peripheral Pulmonary Stenosis. Heart. 2010.
Mullins CE, et al. Peripheral Pulmonary Artery Stenosis: Clinical and Angiographic Features. Circulation. 1988.
